content: 1. Pleurisy root may reduce the effects of estradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 2. Estradiol may decrease the levels of pyridoxine (vitamin B6) by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 3. Estradiol may increase the levels of ropinirole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 4. Estradiol may decrease the levels of rose hips by increasing their elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 5. Estradiol may reduce the effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) such as amitriptyline, trimipramine, or clomipramine, while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and the risk of adverse effects. The mechanism of this interaction is unspecified, and the clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 6. Acetazolamide may increase the levels or effects of estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. Close monitoring is advised. 7. Estradiol may decrease the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially impairing glucose tolerance and reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 8. Amikacin may decrease the levels or effects of estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of estradiol and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 9. Amiodarone may increase the levels or effects of estradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Estradiol may decrease the effects of anastrozole by pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially diminishing the pharmacologic action of anastrozole. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced therapeutic efficacy. 11. Anastrozole may increase the levels or effects of estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 12. Androstenedione may increase the effects of estradiol through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 13. Estradiol may decrease the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III by pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. These interactions are contraindicated. 14. Apalutamide may decrease the levels or effects of estradiol by increasing its elimination or by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. If coadministration is unavoidable, therapeutic effects should be closely monitored, and dose adjustments may be necessary. 15. Aprepitant may increase the levels or effects of estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 16. Estradiol may decrease the effects of argatroban by pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This interaction is contraindicated. 17. Armodafinil may decrease the levels or effects of estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 18. Artemether/lumefantrine may decrease the levels or effects of estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Alternatives should be considered if available. 20. Atorvastatin may increase the levels or effects of estradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of estradiol in accordance with prescribing information. 24. Estradiol may decrease the effects of bemiparin and bivalirudin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. These interactions are contraindicated. 25. Boron may increase the levels of estradiol by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 26. Cannabidiol may affect estradiol levels by inducing or inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Dosage adjustments of CYP1A2 substrates may be necessary. 31. Carbamazepine may decrease the levels or effects of estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 32.
